title: Repair F938/F929 event units for fuel, shields and hull repair
finding: main.rs passes combat::frame_tics into spend_thrust_energy/recharge. F152 divides elapsed tics by 0xc22e and dispatches event 6 through F151 to F1007; F1007 passes the whole-second count to F938. At 1x the port charges about 49,700 times the source rate. This explains early internal-fuel warnings and disabled acceleration.
acceptance: Trace one reserve from fresh type-0 boot through idle, 0x24 climb, full thrust, firing and 1x/10x/10000x. Match source event counts, energy, warning time, limit restoration, shields and repair; preserve wrapping arithmetic.
progress: 2026-10-26: F938/F929 executed-source comparison now passes 192 cases (reserve, shields, hull, wrapping arithmetic, fuel and waste). Whole-second live events retained; exact F152 scheduler alignment remains open. 2026-11-10: F152 ported (ffe_core::second_events): events are (DATA_008804 - DATA_008808) / 0xc22e of the day fraction, the marker moves by whole events and follows the clock in every module (including the hyperspace clock step), not a float 49,700-tic second; the new game's 0x80000000-vs-0 marker gives the source's 43,200-event first dispatch; F208's 10x..10000x selection pulls the marker back one event; the pending fraction is saved. The --state oracle now records DATA_008808 and verify-reference checks it on every in-game frame. The executed --state trace shows the 43,200-event dispatch on the first in-game frame (marker 0 -> 0x7fffd280) and matches all 238 in-game frames. F1007's mode-2 branch is ported: while the autopilot flies (F1020 sets +0xe8 = 2) no F938 runs, so no shield recharge, hull repair, laser cooling or thrust energy; the hull still cools. F1007's +0x10e countdown is ported (flight.rs). 2026-11-17: the reserve (+0x11e) is traced against the executed original (--flight keyboard 900, FFE_RESERVE_DUMP): the 43,200-event first dispatch, every whole-second event and the thrust spend match exactly to frame 484 and within 6 of about 5,600 units to frame 899 (takeoff_replay.rs, port_reserve_follows_the_original). Open: firing and 10x-10000x acceleration traces, the mode-2 per-second autopilot arrival checks (PAR-11) and NPC event-6 handling (PAR-15). 2026-11-18: traced against the executed original. Firing (FFE_FIRE_FROM, the real F931 every frame from 280): refire and laser heat exact on 728 frames and 21 shots, reserve within 6 (Hope 68). F152 events exact on 358 frames through 1x, 10x, 100x, 1000x, 10000x and back (tests/event_replay.rs, FFE_ACCEL_AT). Closed by owner decision as accepted at about 95%; live shield, repair, warning-time and limit-restoration traces were not made (docs/ACCEPTED_PARITY.md).

title: Make reserve refuelling and cargo fuel bookkeeping match F929/F903

title: Use one authoritative fitted-drive and failure state
finding: Damage/service code changes combat.drive while drive_state prefers nonzero loadout.drive. Thus a damaged/destroyed drive can still supply the old hyperdrive class, and reserve fuel selection can disagree with the jump report.
acceptance: Destroy, degrade, service, remove and fit each drive; compare engine limits, gauge, fuel type, range, jump refusal and reload with the original object +0xd0.
progress: 2026-10-26: Jump class now reads object drive state without resurrecting a removed/integral drive from statistics. Damage, degradation, servicing, save migration and escape inheritance agree with that state. Damage/save/outfitting checks pass; full source scenario trace remains.

title: Translate the complete F1013 takeoff handler and same-frame mode order
finding: F1013 runs F1037, changes 0x24 to 0x26 before F1041 when its tests pass, and explicitly calls F602. The port updates Takeoff after its physics tick and Player::step_in normally chooses capped F601 when engines are on. The fixed up-thrust is therefore not sufficient evidence of source launch behaviour.
acceptance: Replay type-0 and type-1 launches: no keys, held Return/Shift or selected port control mapping, speed change at threshold, engine-off and failure cases. Compare every frame mode, set/actual speed, thrust, cap, velocity and position.
progress: 2026-10-26: F1013 now transitions on previous altitude/current set speed before F1041 and always uses uncapped F602, including transition frame. Runtime defers F1031 until the next handler. Boundary and real Hope launch regressions pass; full source frame replay remains. 2026-11-10: tests/takeoff_replay.rs replays the executed --flight takeoff trace frame by frame (Tab at 170, faster held from 260, 21 ms frames) through the game loop's own hand-off. Mode 0x24 at 171 and 0x26 at 261 and every set-speed value match; the launch frame does not move the ship in either. Fixed: F650/F994's pad seat is now made in the port's own (planet rotating) frame and then turned by F1677, as the original does; with the system-frame rows F650's << 10 put the Ross 154 seat 2,048 mm and the Hope seat about 1.8 m off. Both seats now match the original's --geometry within 1 unit. Remaining: the climb runs about 1% slow and F1031 clears 2 frames early (the pad world's linear frame, PAR-05/flight-1); after clearing, the original's acceleration falls with speed while the port's does not (free-flight physics, not F1013). Later on 2026-11-10: the free-flight gap was F1014, which the port never ran in flight. F1021 (mode 0) and F1019 (mode 2) call it after F1033's scan when the contact has bit 0: below 20 km JJFFE's drag takes F1521(v, min(tics,0xffff) << 11) from each velocity component once the speed word (+0xd8) reaches 0xbb8, and its heat runs as in the landed handlers. With it the replay's per-frame acceleration matches the original's within one unit and speed stays within 1.25% to frame 899 (it was 23% fast). The replay is now a regression test: exact set speed and launch/hand-off frames, F1031's clear within two frames, speed within 2%. 2026-11-18: the type-0 (Hope, `--start-key=0x39`) launch now replays like the Ross one (takeoff_replay.rs, FFE_START_TYPE=0): modes, set speed and launch/hand-off frames exact, velocity within 3 units, speed within 0.28% to frame 899, reserve within 12, uneven frames within 1.73% altitude. The port was right: the replay had left out F998's F997 (rows 0 and 2 reversed for type 0), which new_commander applies. The no-key launch (`--flight hover 900`) replays on both starts: the 0x24 to 0x26 hand-off on altitude alone on frames 315 (Hope) and 292 (Ross), velocity within 1. F1013 itself has no engine-off or failure branch (it tests altitude and set speed, then F1037/F1041/F602/F1046/F1033). Two harness cases (`FFE_ENGINES_OFF_AT`, `FFE_LIMITS_CUT_AT`; `--flight` now takes up to 20000 frames) expose differences, so the item stays open: with the engines off at frame 300 the original's velocity steps by about (+26, 0, +37) units in one frame (frame 301, Hope) where the port's barely moves, so F1043's engines-off request (damping toward the combat velocity, DATA_008839..41) is not the original's; with the six thrust limits halved at frame 200 the port tracks the original within 1 unit for 47 frames and 5 units (0.6%) by frame 248. 2026-11-18: closed by owner decision as accepted at about 95% of the original; the gaps left on purpose are in docs/ACCEPTED_PARITY.md.

title: Verify original set-speed controls, input gates and speed persistence end to end
certainty: Confirmed differences; reported dead acceleration also depends on PAR-01
finding: Modern W/S is default while source Return/Shift is selectable. HeldControls adds release gates. Landed F1039 correctly excludes throttle, but launch must enable F1037 immediately. OriginalFlight reconstruction derives nonnegative set speed from actual forward velocity, losing negative or independently selected speed; cancel has both halt-to-zero and actual-speed paths.
implementation: crates/ffe-core/src/keyboard.rs; crates/ffe-rs/src/input.rs (scancode, slow_down, flight_module_active); crates/ffe-rs/src/original_flight.rs (prepare, set_flight_view); crates/ffe-rs/tests/takeoff_replay.rs; crates/ffe-rs/tests/controls.rs
acceptance: Record physical key -> mapped key -> active/mode -> F1121 set speed -> thrust -> actual velocity. Test fresh key after intro, held intro key, launch, autopilot cancel, engines off, reverse speed, menus and reload. Source controls are default; optional mappings belong only in Port Options.
progress: 2026-10-26: Signed selected speed persists independently of actual velocity through save/model rebuild. New settings default to Classic; saved preferences preserved. Remaining input/cancel/source-replay checks are open. 2026-11-02: DATA_008866 is written only by the new-game set-up (0) and read by F1018 and F750, so the autopilot cancel always zeroes the set speed; the port's cancel does that, and OriginalFlight::from_flight's forward-speed fallback applies only to states without a saved set speed (older saves). Key-to-thrust replay checks remain. 2026-11-10: the port never fed DATA_007690 (F1121's held-key scale), so holding Return or Shift raised and lowered the set speed more slowly than the original once held past 0x10 ticks (about a third of a second). ffe_core::keyboard ports Timer50Hz's 50 Hz accumulators, GuiReadAllInput's last-key counter and the platform's initial-press/auto-repeat report; OriginalFlight feeds it every held key's original scancode and takes F1038's steering counts from it. The Classic slow-down key is right Shift only (DATA_007694 is scancode 0x36; left Shift only selects the shifted action table). A new reference scenario (--flight keyboard 900: Return, right Shift through zero and below, Return from negative, A pressed inside a hold) matches the port's set speed on all 730 frames (takeoff_replay.rs); with the scale removed it fails at frame 290. Remaining: menus/reload/autopilot-cancel key paths and the HeldControls release gate in a recorded input replay. Later on 2026-11-10 (done): F1037 runs only while the flight module shows (DATA_008630 < 0; F1006 sets 0x7f when another module takes over). The port fed flight keys under the F2 status screen (module 0x0e) and the map pages; input::flight_module_active now clears Player::active there (the navigation computer and the F5 engines page are the flight module's own and keep it), so Return/Shift and F1038 steering do nothing and the 0x80 latch is untouched. controls.rs replays recorded input lines through HeldControls (EXP-003), the Classic mapping, the module gate, F1037/F1121 and the thrust: a key held through the intro or through F2 needs a fresh press, a fresh Return under F2 does nothing, right Shift stops at zero and a new press reverses, left Shift does nothing, and the selected speed survives a save and reload. Engines off (+0xe9 bit 0) skips the set-speed keys but still steers. Autopilot cancel (2026-11-02), the takeoff and keyboard reference replays complete the acceptance list.

progress: 2026-11-02: the corridor test, 250 m/s limit and teleporting 'pushed clear' are gone from normal flight. Inside an orbital station's hull radius the ship flies in the station's rotating frame for each tick and F569/F570/F575 scan the station's collision stream; F1021/F1024's rule reads the result (region 0x20 with a soft touch 0x40 and no crash: dock when cleared, F1022's warning and the 0x24 climb when not, the pad-1 bay check), and a hull strike is F575's crash/bounce with F953 damage. tests/station_dock.rs: entering the slot on the axis gives 0x22 then 0x62, 120 m off the axis at 200 m/s gives 0x80 outside the region. The autopilot's final-leg roll alignment uses the same spun rows. The station's orbital motion is carried by the navigator's frame following. 2026-11-18: the collision, physics and recharge oracles re-run and pass against the executed original. The harness's --flight dock scenario (launch from Lave Station, then F1020's autopilot back to it, with the docking computer fitted) records the whole dock: the autopilot touches the slot at frame 7660 (mode 0xa) and the stages 0xa, 0xc, 0xe, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18, 0x28 and 0x2a begin on frames 7660, 8100, 8225, 8320, 8446, 8572, 8698, 8824, 8916 and 8917. title: Unify source event clocks, time acceleration and physical integration
finding: The frame loop, fixed prototype accumulator, whole-second events, AI updates and 0.1 s physics clamp use different scheduling paths. TICS_PER_SECOND is 49700 while F152 uses 0xc22e=49710. High acceleration can advance clocks/events without equivalent collision/frame work.
